messages:
juniper: Hey — big issue, customer-facing outage. After we renamed a tool this morning, calls using the new name are 404ing. Example call and response below.

juniper: ```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/toolcall \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"tool":"Invoice_Gen","args":{"order_id":"1234"}}'
```

juniper: Response: `{"error":"tool_not_found","tool":"Invoice_Gen","request_id":"req_01A2B3"}`

juniper: Registry UI shows alias `invoice-gen` and also a legacy `Invoice_Gen` entry (we did the rename via the admin migration). Calls that use the tool UUID succeed, so looks like alias resolution is inconsistent.

maya: Thanks — sorry about the outage. Can you confirm: hosted vs dedicated? region? customer org id? Also paste the request_id (you included one — thanks). I'll open a ticket and ping eng/runtime. :pray:

juniper: Hosted (us-west-2), org: juniper-saas, req id is req_01A2B3. Happening for all our users hitting the public API. Workaround: calling the tool by UUID works: -> returns 200.

maya: created ticket #SUP-12345 and escalated to eng-runtime + SRE. tagging @omar and @liam.

support-bot: Ticket SUP-12345 created: https://redwood.support/SUP-12345 — priority P1.

omar: looking. Quick hypothesis: alias registry and edge cache have divergent key normalization (case-sensitive vs casefold). If migration created `Invoice_Gen` while runtime expects lowercased `invoice-gen` keys, some routing paths can miss and return not_found. Can you grab a stack trace or router logs for one failed request? grep for `alias_lookup` and the request_id.

juniper: Pasted logs: 

juniper: ```
[2026-03-17T12:04:21Z] request=req_01A2B3 incoming tool_lookup alias=Invoice_Gen -> cache MISS
[2026-03-17T12:04:21Z] request=req_01A2B3 registry_lookup name=invoice-gen -> found id=tool_7f9a
[2026-03-17T12:04:21Z] request=req_01A2B3 router.resolve -> lookup_path=/cache/Invoice_Gen -> not found -> respond 404
```

omar: yep that's consistent: registry has the lowercase mapping but the request path used the original-cased alias `Invoice_Gen` and was hitting cache key with case preserved. We have mixed normalization in the router -> cache layer.

liam: paging infra: looks like cache keys were generated by the migration job with original alias casing; runtime normalization changed last month but migration didn't normalize. Short term: we can hotpatch the cache by writing a normalized mapping for that org. I can run a backfill script that copies entries to lowercased keys.

omar: concrete repro for devs: call the same curl with tool name `Invoice_Gen` and with `invoice-gen`. One will 404, the other will 200 (or succeed if using UUID). Also showing the internal GET that returns both entries: 

omar: ```
GET /internal/registry/tools?org=juniper-saas&name=invoice-gen
Response: [{"id":"tool_7f9a","name":"invoice-gen","aliases":["invoice-gen","Invoice_Gen"]}]
```

omar: root cause: migration created an alias duplicate with original-casing and our cache layer treats keys case-sensitively. Fix is to normalize aliases during migration and run a backfill.

liam: I ran the backfill for juniper-saas: created normalized keys and warmed cache for the affected nodes. Rolling out now to the remaining nodes in us-west-2.

liam: Backfill progress: 1/6 nodes complete, 3/6 warming, ETA ~6m.

juniper: any ETA on full fix? We need to update our customers.

omar: short-term mitigations: (1) use tool UUID (works), (2) add a temporary alias via admin UI with the exact case used by your clients, or (3) wait for backfill to finish (liam). We'll cut a proper fix to normalize aliases in migration code and deploy in next patch (tomorrow morning).

maya: keeping customer updated. adding note to SUP-12345 with workaround steps. :white_check_mark:

liam: backfill complete on all nodes in region. Confirmed requests with `Invoice_Gen` now hit the normalized cache and return 200.

juniper: Confirmed — calls succeed now. Thanks everyone, please leave the ticket open until migration change is shipped.

omar: will follow up with an RFC + migration PR. Will include a post-mortem blurb re: case normalization and add regression test around alias collisions.

support-bot: SUP-12345 updated: status=investigating -> mitigated.

juniper: Appreciated.
